title: Cell Culture and Estimation of Cytokines by ELISA
author: Mohd Khubaib
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.p2hdqb6

steps.title: Seed and treat RAW264.7 cells
steps.instruction: Plate 0.1 × 10⁶ RAW264.7 cells per well in a 96‑well plate, add native or heat‑inactivated recombinant protein at the desired concentrations, incubate for 24 h, then harvest the culture supernatant.

steps.title: Seed and treat splenocytes
steps.instruction: Plate 0.1 × 10⁶ splenocytes per well in DMEM in a 96‑well plate, add recombinant protein at the desired concentrations, incubate for 72 h, collect the supernatant and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Perform mouse cytokine ELISA
steps.instruction: Measure mouse TNF‑α, IFN‑γ, IL‑10 and IL‑6 in the collected supernatants using OptEIA kits (BD Biosciences) following the steps below.

substeps.instruction: Coat 96‑well ELISA plates with capture antibody in coating buffer (bicarbonate/phosphate buffer) and incubate at 4 °C overnight.
Wash plates three times with PBS‑T (0.05 % Tween‑20).
Block with 10 % fetal bovine serum (FBS) for 1 h (also serves as assay diluent).
Add standards and supernatant samples; incubate 2 h at room temperature.
Wash plates five times with PBS‑T.
Add detection antibody and enzyme conjugate; incubate 1 h.
Wash plates seven times with PBS‑T.
Add TMB substrate, develop, then stop the reaction with 2 N H₂SO₄.
Read absorbance at 450 nm and calculate cytokine concentrations using the standard curve.

steps.title: Perform human cytokine ELISA
steps.instruction: Measure human TNF‑α and IL‑6 in the same supernatants using Peprotech ELISA development kits, following the manufacturer’s protocol (identical to the mouse ELISA steps above).

steps.title: Collect mouse serum for B‑cell ELISA
steps.instruction: Bleed mice via the lateral tail vein, collect blood, allow clotting, centrifuge to obtain serum, and store serum at –20 °C until use.

steps.title: B‑cell IgG subclass ELISA
steps.instruction: Determine IgG1, IgG2a and IgG2b responses to individual proteins using ELISA as described below.

substeps.instruction: Coat 96‑well plates with the specific protein diluted in PBS to 10 µg ml⁻¹; incubate at 4 °C overnight.
Wash plates three times with wash buffer.
Block plates for 1 h at room temperature (no specific blocker stated; use the same blocking solution as above if desired).
Wash three times, then add serum diluted 1:100; incubate 2 h at room temperature.
Wash three times, add secondary conjugate antibodies: IgG1 at 1:5 000, IgG2a at 1:3 000, IgG2b at 1:3 000; incubate 1 h.
Wash at least five times, add TMB substrate, develop, and stop the reaction with 2 N H₂SO₄.
Read absorbance at 450 nm and calculate IgG subclass levels using appropriate standards.
